title: One affine weakly contractible cover of a quasi-compact pro-etale object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For every object $T\to X$ whose scheme $T$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], there exists a covering family consisting of one morphism $V\to T$, where $V$ is affine and weakly contractible in the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Here weakly contractible means that for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on this site, $F(V)\to G(V)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0F4P, lemma-weakly-contractible-cover, last sentence; Tag 090L (sites.tex, definition-w-contractible), condition (2) of Tag 090K (lemma-w-contractible)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family], choose a covering family $\{U_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ whose members are affine and weakly contractible for the full site.

Choose a finite affine open cover of T (Scheme.affineCover followed by OpenCover.finiteSubcover). Pull the given weakly etale covering family back over each chart. QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom supplies a finite affine refinement of each pullback. On an affine target, such a finite affine covering is quasi-compact. Bind these refinements with the finite affine open cover, obtaining a finite quasi-compact weakly etale covering W_j of T and a refinement map to the original family. This is the private, fully proved Lean helper exists_finite_refinement; it requires no quasi-separatedness of T. Retain the original affine weakly contractible objects indexed by the refinement map (repetition is harmless).

source.place: Tag 0F4P, lemma-weakly-contractible-cover, finite-subfamily paragraph; elementary finite-witness argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation] directly to the retained finite family; affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It gives an affine object W, inclusions, and the coproduct universal property for their representable sheaves. Descend the original covering arrows using that coproduct universal property and the full faithfulness of the subcanonical lifted Yoneda functor, obtaining g : W -> T whose composite with each inclusion is the original arrow. The finite quasi-compact refinement of step 2 consequently refines the singleton g. QuasiCompactCover.of_hom proves its quasi-compact covering condition; the same factorization proves surjectivity. The underlying arrow is weakly etale because its composite with T -> X is W -> X and WeaklyEtale.of_comp cancels the weakly etale structural arrow. Thus the singleton belongs to the pro-etale precoverage [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering].

source.place: Tag 0F4P, disjoint-union paragraph; Tag 09A1, qcqs subsite paragraph

proof.text: For an epimorphism F -> G and a section s of G over W, use the section-product bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation]. Weak contractibility of every retained original object supplies a preimage of the restriction of s on each summand. Surjectivity of the product comparison for F glues this tuple to a section a over W. Naturality of the comparison and its injectivity for G show that the image of a is s. The argument includes the empty index type without a separate choice of an element: the dependent tuple and its gluing still exist.
